rationale: Interpreting the measurement case and correcting two statements the receipt contradicts. CheckRun 84fd61ba7e8240c8aff44e0559fa7ec4 (exit 0) evaluated its comparison and it is violated with a complete witness, and its event reports `origin_promise_pid` 3 with `origin_phase_accept` true alongside `decided_after_resync` 0 after a 30.1 s wait. That means the origin was re-prepared and re-synchronised - its promise moved to the new leader and it entered the accept phase, which happens only through an `AcceptSync` - and its decided index stayed 0 because that `AcceptSync` carried decided index 0, the new leader itself having decided nothing in this construction. So the counterevidence sentence I recorded two turns ago ('this scenario does not exercise a completed re-synchronisation at all') and the matching limitation are both wrong as written: the re-synchronisation happens, it simply carries no decided progress. I am correcting the account and the knowledge entry's conditions rather than leaving statements the receipt contradicts, and I state the remaining open item as why the new leader never decides its own entry here, since that is what a construction exercising a progress-carrying re-synchronisation would need.

investigations.discriminator: The band and the re-synchronisation's occurrence are now measured; the open item is why the new leader never decides its own entry in this construction, which is what prevents any retained run from exhibiting a re-synchronisation that both completes and advances the decided index. A construction in which that entry is decided (for instance re-electing the origin later, or letting the new leader reach a write quorum) would exercise that and could change what the endpoints imply about where the stale placeholders come from.

knowledge.statement: When a truncation discards entries whose deferred placeholders in `unconfirmed_local` are still queued, those placeholders keep their position in the queue and are consumed by later index advances, so the index reported for a later caller is shifted upward by the number of discarded entries. Retained runs of the same scenario at four tick periods: at 100 and 250 ms the fresh call resolved `ok` with index 2, which is where entry 33 sits; at 500 and 1000 ms it resolved `ok` with an index two positions beyond entry 33 (index 4 while the entry sits at index 2, or index 3 while it sits at index 1) with the returned index holding entry 35. A separation run that polled the origin's decided index for 30.1 s before re-electing it found that index still 0 and delivered the same shift; in that run the origin's promise had moved to the new leader and its phase was Accept, so the re-synchronisation had happened and simply carried no decided progress.
knowledge.conditions: Actor layer with batch_size 3, three-node cluster, majority quorum, the leader cut off from both followers, the followers taking over with node 3, the origin re-elected explicitly, and a fresh `append_notify` filling the batch with two filler appends. Retained evidence covers tick periods 100, 250, 500 and 1000 ms plus a 1000 ms run that measured the origin's promise and phase. The origin's decided index stays at 0 throughout because the new leader never decides its own entry in this construction, so no retained run exhibits a re-synchronisation that both completes and advances the decided index; the internal placeholder queue is unobservable through the public API, so the queue accounting is the mechanism the endpoints imply rather than a direct observation.
knowledge.changed_premise: The conditions no longer say that this scenario leaves the origin's re-synchronisation unexercised. A measurement case shows the origin's promise pointing at the new leader with its phase in Accept while its decided index is still 0 after a 30.1 s wait, so the re-synchronisation does happen and carries no decided progress because the new leader had decided nothing. The statement is otherwise unchanged; the executions gained that case's receipt.

interpretations.rationale: Current account of the second mechanism, with the re-synchronisation question settled by measurement. Deferred writes are tracked as one placeholder per buffered entry in `unconfirmed_local`, `reconcile_unconfirmed` consumes one placeholder per unit of accepted-index advance in queue order, and a placeholder whose buffered ballot no longer matches the current promise is discarded while still consuming its advance. In this scenario the origin buffers two entries, loses the followers to node 3, is re-elected, and then buffers a fresh `append_notify` with two filler appends; across the retained runs at 100, 250, 500 and 1000 ms ticks the fresh call returned the correct index at the two smaller periods and an index two positions beyond the entry at the two larger ones, with the returned index holding entry 35 - the same violation reproduced at 1000 ms three times. The diagnostic run adds that the origin was in fact re-prepared and re-synchronised (its promise pointed at the new leader and its phase was Accept) while its decided index remained 0 after a thirty-second wait, which locates the reason for that index in the new leader having decided nothing rather than in the origin failing to re-synchronise. That corrects two statements from earlier accounts: the re-synchronisation is exercised, and the phase field I misread as a confound is simply a consequence of the new leader's own entry not being decided. What remains unobserved is therefore narrower than before - not whether the origin re-synchronises, but where exactly the stale placeholders that shift the index come from, in a construction where the origin's decided index never advances.
counterevidence: The origin's decided index never advanced past 0 in any retained run, because the new leader never decides its own entry in this construction; no retained run therefore exhibits a re-synchronisation that both completes and advances the decided index, so the intermediate steps of the mechanism remain unobserved even though the caller-visible violation is complete and reproduced.
The placeholder queue is unobservable through the public API, so the queue accounting is the explanation the endpoints imply rather than a direct measurement.

The batch size is fixed at 3, the tick periods are four points, and the origin is always the leader in these runs; follower origins, other deferral patterns and the interaction with the arm-order defect are unmeasured.
A caller that re-reads the decided log at the returned index and compares values is not misled, the mitigation the Superseded variant's documentation already suggests.
limitations: Four tick periods, one schedule each at 100, 250 and 500 ms and three at 1000 ms; the boundary between 250 and 500 ms is not located.
Three-node cluster, majority quorum, in-process transport; no crash recovery, so nothing here extends to restart-time pending state.
The new leader's own entry is never decided in this construction, so the receipts do not cover the case where a re-synchronisation carries decided progress.
interpretations.joint_history: The first receipt is the tick-period sweep; the second is the next revision of the same fixed experiment, whose scenario, batch size, election and resend tick counts, poll flag and tick periods are unchanged and which adds only two read-only measurements of the origin's own reported state at the re-synchronisation sample. Both were executed from their saved inputs, so they can be read as one band plus one diagnostic of the same construction.
